parsed.why: Strong state protections: shield law, gender-identity anti-discrimination, hate-crime coverage, X markers, care coverage. National border/entry regime remains limiting; documented birth-sex custody practice and no current custody-identity protocol pull it below the most protective peers.

Most Protective tier with shield law, broad anti-discrimination, strengthened hate-crime law, X markers, and explicit custody treatment by gender identity. Strong local protections raise it well above parent, but national passport/entry and facility regime still caps it.

Adds hostile school/college birth-certificate facility law, restricted DMV markers, and care/sports bans in litigation, plus no statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination. But facility law has no enforcement mechanism and mostly affects students, so only modestly below parent.

Worst local layer: birth-certificate changes effectively closed, explicit state-run bathroom restrictions, care and sports bans, anti-trans school disclosure, and no gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination coverage. State-imposed facility exposure makes it materially below parent.

Most Protective tier with shield law, broad public-accommodations anti-discrimination, easy X markers, gender-neutral single-occupancy restroom rule, hate-crime coverage, and panic-defense repeal. Lacks a documented custody-identity protocol; national border/entry regime still limits.
